claims.text: The artifacts describe one and the same trip, and on this trip's own trace a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00115, and the trace's first fix at 21:10:00 matches the recorded start of the trip. Measured from the trace polyline — the governing field under POL-RD-01 — the vehicle covered 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km or 25.8%. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass: 25.8% exceeds the 20% threshold and 5.78 km exceeds the 0.8 km threshold. The trip_record's rounded 28.2 km is not cited for the threshold; the trace figure is.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — quoted_fare_sgd 34.50, fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE — so POL-RD-11 governs and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. That does not leave the driver keeping the whole fare: POL-RD-11 limits the rider's remedy to the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. Charged_total is 39.00; the quote is 34.50; the difference of 4.50 is made up entirely of the two ERP lines on the fare breakdown. That 4.50 is the pool the rider can recover from, and the next claims show 2.00 of it must come back.

The $2.00 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' line is a phantom charge and is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction. The gantry sits at 1.287, 103.806 and is not on the optimal route; the closest the trace ever comes to it is 5,419 m, at the very first fix of the trip. POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing, and the vehicle was never within sixteen times that radius. POL-RD-09(4) makes this refundable whether or not a deviation exists, so it stands independently of the distance question.

Reconciling the fare on the record yields exactly the sum the rider is owed. The only properly chargeable gantry is the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) pass at $2.50: it lies on the booked optimal route and the trace passes within 44.5 m of it at 21:32:40, comfortably inside the 250 m match radius. The arithmetic is therefore charged_total 39.00, less the 34.50 quote, less the 2.50 KPE pass the rider did in fact incur, less waiting_time_fee 0.00 — leaving $2.00 owing to the rider, with the phantom AYE line removed.

The driver's traffic excuse cannot exonerate the detour. POL-RD-03 requires a traffic_advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses. EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING: the identifier carries no payload, weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, whose own detail records that no LTA advisory covers the CTE, the KPE or the TPE in the 21:06–21:48 window. There is accordingly no advisory to name the affected segment, no validity window to overlap the trip, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km from which a capped justified excess could be computed. The driver's bare 'CTE northbound was heavy' is precisely the general assertion that POL-RD-08 says does not discharge the burden of pointing to a specific artifact and clause.

The chat log does not shift the cost onto the rider. POL-RD-04 exonerates only an instruction that comes from the rider. The only message proposing the KPE–TPE route is the driver's, sent at 21:14:10; the rider's single reply, 'ok' at 21:14:50, names no road and no waypoint and its waypoint_hint is null. A message from the driver, acknowledged without any place or road being identified, is not a rider instruction, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to the driver and the 5.78 km of excess remains unjustified.

Nothing on this record compels escalation, and a terminal escalation would only hold the disputed amount rather than return it. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 100% coverage, 229 fixes, no gaps, and a maximum consecutive-fix gap of 0 seconds against a 90-second limb (a) threshold, so limbs (a), (b) and (c) never fire. POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered by the unmatched AYE line, because that line is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts and POL-RD-09(4) expressly says does not engage POL-RD-10(8). The trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match and the timestamps agree, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire either.

No extra corroboration burden attaches to the rider here. POL-RD-08's additional-corroboration condition requires deviation_claims_60d of 4 or more with deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 1 or fewer; the rider's profile shows 0 and 0. The trace alone therefore carries the excess, and the rider's threshold case is complete on limbs (a) and (b) of POL-RD-08.

claims.text: This trip is an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare: the fare_breakdown carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 and null per-km and per-minute rates because there is no meter. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and the rider is already whole on distance and time — so her request to 'refund the extra distance' is unavailable to her however long the route actually driven, and the driver cannot be charged for it.

On an upfront-quoted trip the rider's only monetary remedy is the amount by which charged_total (39.00) exceeds quoted_fare_sgd (34.50) plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. That gap is exactly 4.50, which is precisely the two billed ERP lines (2.50 KPE + 2.00 AYE) — so there is no distance or time overcharge anywhere in this fare, and nothing beyond the pass-through lines can be owed.

The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) charge of 2.50 is properly chargeable and must not be refunded: it lies on the optimal route (on_optimal_route true) and the driver's own trace passes within 44.5 m of the gantry at 21:32:40, comfortably inside the 250 m crossing radius POL-RD-09 sets for matching a gantry to the trace.

I do not contest the AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of 2.00: the closest the trace ever comes to that gantry is 5,419 m and the gantry is not on the optimal route, so it is an unmatched billing line that POL-RD-09(4) refunds in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. That defect is the ledger's, not the driver's — his own trace and his own statement both put him nowhere near the AYE — so it supports a billing-integrity referral only, and the correction is capped at that single 2.00 line.

Even taking the deviation as established on the trace (excess 5.78 km, 25.8% of optimal), it is NOT a MATERIAL deviation: the material gates are 8.0 km and 50% of optimal and neither is met, so POL-RD-06's mandatory driver-profile check is not triggered by materiality. In any event the driver's 90-day record is 1 deviation flag over 523 completed trips (0.19%), nowhere near the 3-flag or 5% pattern thresholds, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists and no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral can follow from it.

Nothing in this record warrants escalation. The trace is unimpaired — 100% coverage, 229 fixes at a steady 10 s sample interval, no gaps and a 0 s maximum gap — so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire; the trip identifier TRP-00115 matches across the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown and their timestamps are consistent, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire; and the only unmatched fare line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes from escalation. The dispute should be ruled on the merits rather than held.

The driver's case does not rest on any traffic advisory, so the absent advisory EV-ADVIS-00115-01 (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — no LTA advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE in the 21:06-21:48 window) is immaterial: no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. The driver relies on POL-RD-11, which needs no advisory at all.

No driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) is warranted: no pattern is established under POL-RD-06, the deviation is not material, and the driver disclosed the reroute in the app at 21:14:10 ('CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE') which the rider acknowledged at 21:14:50 — the opposite of concealment. That exchange is not a rider instruction identifying a place or road, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to either side, but it shows the driver acted openly rather than hiding a detour.

ruling.explanation: To the rider: you are right that the route driven was longer than the booked route, and you are owed a refund — but not for the reason you filed. Your fare was an UPFRONT_QUOTE ($34.50 fixed at booking; per-km and per-minute rates are null because there is no meter). Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were locked at booking, so the extra kilometres cost you nothing on those lines and there is no distance refund available however long the detour was; POL-RD-02 does not run on an upfront trip. That part of your claim is rejected, outweighed by POL-RD-11. What you are owed is $2.00, and it is owed under POL-RD-09(4). Your receipt bills $2.00 for the 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' gantry, but the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00115) never comes closer than 5,419 m to it — more than twenty times the 250 m crossing radius the clause sets. That is a phantom line and is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction, whether or not any deviation exists. The other gantry, KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) at $2.50, is properly chargeable: it lies on your optimal route and the trace passes within 44.5 m of it, so it is not refunded. The arithmetic is charged_total $39.00 less the $34.50 quote less the $2.50 KPE pass = $2.00. Note the $2.00 is not added on top of any distance refund — there is none — and the two ERP lines are not counted twice. To the driver: no adverse conduct finding is made against you. The deviation is established on this trip's own trace under POL-RD-01 — 28.18 km driven against a 22.4 km optimal, an excess of 5.78 km or 25.8%, clearing both the 20% and 0.8 km gates — but it is not MATERIAL (short of 8.0 km and 50%), and because the fare was fixed you are not charged for the excess. You disclosed the re-route in-app at 21:14:10 and the rider acknowledged at 21:14:50, so there is no concealment; and the POL-RD-06 profile check shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 1 over completed_trips_90d 523, far below the 3-flag and 5% thresholds), so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral follow. The $2.00 AYE line is the ledger's error, not yours — your own trace and your own statement both put you nowhere near that gantry. Your 'CTE northbound was heavy' assertion cannot exonerate any of the route because there is no traffic advisory on the record (EV-ADVIS-00115-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT); that is a bare traffic assertion, and POL-RD-08 says such an assertion, unsupported by an advisory ID, does not discharge the burden. It makes no difference to the money here because POL-RD-11 needs no advisory and no distance refund was ever on the table. The rider's reply 'ok' is not a rider instruction naming a place or road (waypoint_hint null), so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to both sides. Escalation does not fire: the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 229 fixes, 0 s maximum gap), the trip identifier TRP-00115 and its timestamps match across the record, and the only unmatched fare line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. On an upfront fare a detour costs the rider nothing and is not recoverable from them; no driver compensation arises. Ruling: $2.00 refunded to the rider; the remaining $37.00 of the charge stands.

ruling.explanation: To the rider and the driver: this was an upfront-quoted trip. The rider was quoted $34.50 and the distance and time charge was fixed at booking, so under POL-RD-11 no part of the distance or time charge can be refunded however far the car actually drove. That disposes of the request to refund the 'extra distance': the excess is real — the trace covers 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km / 25.8%, so a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 on both gates — but on an upfront fare a longer route costs the rider nothing on distance and time. What the rider paid on top of the quote was $4.50 of ERP: two gantry lines of $2.50 and $2.00. The $2.50 KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) charge stands — that gantry lies on the optimal route and the trace (229 fixes, 100% coverage) passes within 44.5 m of it at 21:32:40, well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses. The $2.00 AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) charge does not stand — that gantry is not on the optimal route and the closest the trace ever comes to it is 5,419 m, more than twenty times the match radius. It is a phantom line, refunded in full by POL-RD-09(4) as a billing-integrity correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The refund is therefore $2.00, reached on two routes that are the same money and are not double-counted: charged $39.00 less the $34.50 quote less the $2.50 properly chargeable KPE pass (POL-RD-11), and equally the unmatched AYE line itself (POL-RD-09(4)). ruling.explanation:
To the rider: you are half right. On the trip's own GPS trace the vehicle covered 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km — an excess of 5.78 km, or 25.8% — which clears both POL-RD-01 gates, so a route deviation is established and the driver's longer route is confirmed. But this was an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare (quoted 34.50), and under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking: the detour cost you nothing on those lines. Your request to 'refund the extra distance' is therefore refused, however far the car actually went; the loss on distance falls on the driver, not on you. What you can recover is what you were charged above the quote plus the pass-throughs you actually incurred. You paid 39.00. The quote is 34.50, and the only gantry the trace shows you crossing is the KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) at 2.50 — the trace passes within 44.5 m of it, so that toll is properly chargeable. That leaves 2.00, which is exactly the 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' line. Your trace never goes near that gantry (closest approach 5,419 m, over twenty times the 250 m crossing radius) and the gantry is not on the optimal route, so the line is a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4): refundable in full, whether or not a deviation exists. We refund SGD 2.00 to you.

To the driver: the KPE toll is properly yours and stays. Your in-app message about heavy CTE traffic and taking the KPE/TPE does not exonerate the extra distance: POL-RD-03 requires a traffic advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses, and there is none — the only advisory in the record, EV-ADVIS-00115-01, is MISSING (no LTA advisory covers the CTE, KPE or TPE in the 21:06–21:48 window), so your general 'traffic was heavy' assertion cannot discharge the burden POL-RD-08 places on you. It makes no difference to the money here, because on an upfront fare no distance charge turns on it. Your 90-day record (1 deviation flag across 523 completed trips, 0.19%) is far below the POL-RD-06 pattern thresholds of 3 flags or 5%, and the deviation is not material (under 8.0 km and under 50%), so there is no repeat-pattern uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The B and the AYE line are not your doing — your own trace and your own statement both put you nowhere near that gantry — so that line is treated as a ledger billing-integrity issue, referred accordingly, and not as misconduct by you.

On the evidence generally: every artifact this ruling rests on — the trip record, the 100%-coverage GPS trace (229 fixes, no gaps, 0 s maximum gap) and the fare breakdown — is admissible at full weight 1.0, and the trip identifier and timestamps agree across them. Nothing in the record triggers mandatory escalation under POL-RD-10, so the case is decided on its merits rather than held. Arithmetic: charged_total 39.00, less quoted fare 34.50, less the properly chargeable KPE pass 2.50, less waiting time 0.00 = 2.00 refunded; the phantom AYE line of 2.00 is not counted twice.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral: the SGD 2.00 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' ERP line was charged for a gantry the trip's GPS trace never approaches (closest fix 5,419 m, against the 250 m match radius). The line is refunded in full and the fare ledger is referred for billing-integrity review.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the mechanics here, and so does the record. This was an upfront-quoted trip (quoted fare SGD 34.50, fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE on the fare breakdown), so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and no distance refund is available however much road was driven. The trace does show 28.18 km against a 22.4 km optimal route - an excess of 5.78 km, 25.8%, which passes both POL-RD-01 establishment gates (20% and 0.8 km) - but on an upfront fare that excess produces no money for the rider. It is also below the materiality gates of 50% and 8.0 km, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation, and the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check, the FULL_REFUND uplift and the POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral do not arise. In any event the driver's 90-day record (1 deviation flag over 523 completed trips, 0.19%) shows no pattern.

You were charged SGD 39.00, which is SGD 4.50 above the quote, and that SGD 4.50 is exactly the two ERP lines. The KPE (Defu Flyover towards ECP) pass of SGD 2.50 was genuinely crossed - the trace passes within 44.5 m of that gantry, which also lies on the booked optimal route - so it is properly chargeable and stays. The AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas) line of SGD 2.00 is a phantom: the trace never comes closer than 5,419 m to that gantry, and the gantry is not on the optimal route. Under POL-RD-09(4) that line is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The refund is therefore charged_total 39.00 less the 34.50 quote less the 2.50 KPE pass actually incurred = SGD 2.00, and it is rounded up to the nearest 0.05 as the policy requires.

Why this is not escalated. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes - 100% coverage, 229 fixes, no gaps, 0 s maximum consecutive-fix gap - so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire; the trip identifiers and timestamps match across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) do not fire; and the only unmatched charge line is the AYE line, which is refunded under POL-RD-09(4), a limb POL-RD-10(8) expressly excepts. On the driver's side, the absent LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-00115-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) is immaterial: the driver's case rests on POL-RD-11, which needs no advisory, and no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. A bare assertion that traffic was heavy, without an advisory ID, does not discharge any burden under POL-RD-08, but it also does not escalate.

The chat exchange ('CTE very heavy boss, i go KPE then TPE' at 21:14:10, acknowledged 'ok' at 21:14:50) is not a rider instruction identifying a place or road and its waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable to either side, as the admissibility note records. No distance or time overcharge exists on this fare, and no driver compensation is due: the fare carries no billed distance for a shortfall to arise, and the unrecovered cost of an unjustified detour on an upfront trip is not recoverable from the rider under POL-RD-11.

The rider's request for the 'extra distance' is refused because the upfront quote already fixes those lines; the rider's request for the AYE ERP is granted in full. The SGD 2.00 AYE line is referred under POL-RD-09(4) as a billing-integrity finding.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 2.00 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' gantry line was charged on a trip whose GPS trace never comes within 250 m of that gantry (nearest fix 5,419 m) and which is not on the booked optimal route. The line is refunded in full as a standalone correction and is referred for billing-integrity review.

Measured from the trace polyline — the governing field under POL-RD-01 — the vehicle covered 28.18 km against a booked optimal of 22.4 km, an excess of 5.78 km or 25.8%. This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip — quoted_fare_sgd 34.50, fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE — so POL-RD-11 governs and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. That does not leave the driver keeping the whole fare: POL-RD-11 limits the rider's remedy to the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. Charged_total is 39.00; the quote is 34.50; the difference of 4.50 is made up entirely of the two ERP lines on the fare breakdown. That 4.50 is the pool the rider can recover from, and the next claims show 2.00 of it must come back.

The $2.00 'AYE (Alexandra Rd towards Tuas)' line is a phantom charge and is refunded in full as a standalone billing-integrity correction. The gantry sits at 1.287, 103.806 and is not on the optimal route; the closest the trace ever comes to it is 5,419 m, at the very first fix of the trip. POL-RD-09(4) matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing, and the vehicle was never within sixteen times that radius.
